lede: The biggest thing on the calendar this week is the San Miguel County commissioners sitting for public hearings on four Land Use Code amendments that would add an entirely new Natural Resources article to county code — covering forestry, oil and gas, and geothermal operations — and that's the kind of foundational change worth showing up for. Telluride's Planning and Zoning Commission also finally gets its crack at the Shandoka Lot Redevelopment PUD on town-owned land at 860 Black Bear Rd, after the hearing was pushed from September. Meanwhile, the school board revisits the mill levy override discussion, the Fire District opens its 2027 budget process, and the hospital district weighs a Two Site Model that could reshape how care is delivered here for years to come.
